items.note: Story 1: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery 1891.
Article VII quoted: paid on butterfat found by test, not weight, and the station's test governs.
Falke's point given: under payment by weight nothing here would have cost any man a dollar.
Effie Loomis secretary 1901, Wilbur Teague bookkeeper 1905, Hobart Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green.
Section A gives 'Selby Vose, manager 1913-1938' but nowhere inside the eight reconstructions states he was Gideon's son; the sonship appears only at B3/E10, which cannot travel into A.
Story 5: the station-gain line, 1898 entry as type, five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account.
Station seven miles up (Story 1), built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Weighing, ten-day composite per patron, charge to the pipette mark, fat column read on the bottle neck; cream down, skim back.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice reproduced in full: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93.
Story 2: 'the same nineteen hundredths in the flush of June as in the depth of February.'
Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / that there was none in the county; the equivalent point appears only in F1.
Keddie b.1861 d.1934, twenty-nine seasons, test book 4 May 1896-31 Dec 1924, dismissed 30 April 1925. (The stray 'went up in 1895' is charged as a corruption deduction, not here.)
Bench routine given in detail and the test book kept in one hand for twenty-nine seasons.
Summary leaf: 1896 part-season 3.80; 3.61 from 1898, within three hundredths every year; step at the change of glassware.
8 May broken pipette, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the nine weeks, return to 3.61, question mark.
Orra was Emmet Brant's sister; Brant the largest patron on Hessel Bottom.
1919 water circular over the manager's signature (Story 6) and Keddie's statement 'I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are' (Story 7).
Died February 1934 with the imputation on him; test book to the County Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Section A mentions the weigh book only as an exhibit and as a record Ivy assembled; the 1 Jan 1897 start and the agreement of the two scales appear only in D2/E21.
Complaints from 1902; Larrow Green 3.78 vs station 3.61 (0.17) kept properly distinct from the 0.19 shortfall.
1908 Grigg committee, Jan-Feb-Mar sampling, wet-hay finding reported as a finding and then defeated.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss across herds appear only in C2/F1, not inside the eight reconstructions.
Story 8: weigh book lent by Roy Brant to Ivy in 1958, with the word 'lent' insisted on.
No Alder Corners narrative in Section A: Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in the eight stories.
The four Hessel Bottom patrons hauling there from 1915 in the summer flush is absent from Section A.
REQUIRED two of four independence elements; Section A gives only 'Rosalie Cudd's Alder Corners figures' (the artifact), no other county, bench, glassware or uncompared book.
Story 6: the same cows off the same wet ground tested 3.78-3.82 at Alder Corners for sixteen seasons, against the station's 3.61.

No separate statement of what the comparison disposes of (same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings, killing hay and watering together); the single Alder Corners sentence is already credited at A5.4 and cannot be scored twice.
Rosalie Cudd named in Section A as copying the figures for Ivy, but not as Jerome's daughter; the daughter relation is the item's discriminating element.
Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, circuit 'from 1907' (correct against the 1908 pair). End year 1936 given only at E26; core fact allowed.
Lactometer at every visit from 1907, never once found water at that station, told the manager so in 1919.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole lot condemned.
Section A never states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Ordered 28 June, Ammon's letter 2 July 1923, glass replaced from July, 1924 average 3.80.
Crate to the station loft; Strawn's notebooks at Farland since 1947, unasked for in the interval.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sittings, second and third in the station's weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), the 1908 hay report read in; none accepted.
Four books named including Strawn's 1923 notebook lying on the table, read for its other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, 'without admission', charged to the station account.
'One fifth of what had been lost' charged to the station account, with $19,000 and the station-gain account established in Story 5.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland, Prof. Leland Vaught.
Five record sets put in one room for the first time in sixty years, all five named.
February 1958, the crate in the loft under a tarpaulin, nine survivors.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings, mean 16.72 against 17.6, '95 hundredths of the mark'; short 0.88 given in Story 3.
Bulletin quote: 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 low by one part in twenty; 3.61 where the milk was 3.80, deficiency nineteen hundredths.
All four inside Section A: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922 (and 1.6M/yr), 76,000 lb, about $19,000, and the ledger identity via the Bulletin's 'stands credited ... as station gain'.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; thirty-five years from the condemnation, thirty-three from the dismissal, twenty-four years dead.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan; notes the two 'great-niece' carriers share one press release and Falke's retraction.
Second cousins with the full pedigree derivation.

A08 abstained: 'On balance I prefer Roy ... but the point is not settled - and it does not disturb the cousin arithmetic either way' (lean with the declining qualifier attached); E28 also says cannot be settled.
Son of Gideon, with the minute-book/self-identification/family sources.
Gideon wrote the rule that made the test the paymaster; the office ran father to son to 1938 and the accuser enforced it.

A01 abstained: headline is 'no established relationship', and 'Treat the two families as unrelated; strictly, the sources establish no connection rather than proving a negative' carries the declining qualifier in the same sentence.
States what is established: Oram's untraceable hearsay chain vs Duncan's traced denial, nothing on paper either way.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, short one part in twenty; 16.27 explicitly rejected.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, noted as 5 percent of 3.80.
76,000 lb, shown both ways.
$19,000; $3,800 / $19,000 = 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction.
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the $90 alternative correctly labelled as the long-run average.
76,000 lb = 5.00 percent of fat delivered and 5.26 percent of fat credited, denominators named, and the Bulletin's mislabel called out (no NT-20 exposure).
$77.93 with the column addition; $77.39 identified as a transposition.
72 pipettes (6 doz), each short 0.88 c.c.
1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923, twenty-six years and about six weeks, against twenty-five full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason.
A02 abstained: verdict sentence is 'Cannot be determined from the sources'; the lean to Sill is explicitly an estimate.
Variable named: the measuring pipette and nothing else, dated at both ends and corroborated by Orra's diary.
Far more than three constants: herds, pasture, season, tester, method, bottles, acid, scales, separator, supervision.
3.61 to 3.80 through nine weeks and back on 10 July.
Both halves: causation by intervention exonerating everyone at the station, plus explicit limits (not the lender, not the total loss, not the reason, nothing about winter feeding).
Sill's scale, the ledgers (with Rundle's retraction), the 1911 interval, plus Brant's weigh book - four attributed reasons across several narrators.
Independence argued by source, place and kind, and reasons 1, 2 and 4 named as surviving without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: headline verdict 'No.' on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries. Gullibility deduction applied.
Literal question answered yes, with 1902 complaints, the 1908 committee, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five present: manager from 1913, signed the annual sheets carrying the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular (also the watering argument at the hearing).
A03 declined in terms: 'the sources do not settle it, and I decline to say he did'; the closing lean is 'incurious rather than complicit', which is not an understatement verdict.

Capped. Well over three keyed rows resolved with method: 1924 average 3.80 by arithmetic, Grigg Jan-Mar by the report over its own letter, six farms, the loft, Ammon's 1897 invoice against 'nothing before 1900', the station-gain line's 1898 origin, sixteen Alder Corners seasons, Vose manager 1913, two bodies not one, weigh book 1 Jan 1897.

Capped. A dedicated near-tie section naming the paired carriers and the breaker: 16.27 (NT-1), 12 July (NT-11, broken by the 28 June order), $77.39 handled at C4a, $3,500, eleven pipettes, five dozen, six weeks, 44M, 3.16, nephew, great-niece, 3.85.

A06 declined with what is established (Story 4 and E22); A10 declined with the by-laws' undated text and the lost 1889-92 minute book (stated in Story 1). A04 not credited - the reground-mold accident is asserted as fact in Story 3, F1 and D1. Bucket does not affect the section total, which is capped.

A whole subsection of self-refuting narrators: Grigg's letter vs his own report, Rundle's note in press, Falke's withdrawal, Bulletin 471 against itself, Junia Ammon's total, Nym's transposed headings, Kyle's 1911/quarter-century, Keddie's Ashlin vs Larrow Green.
Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8.

Full causal chain: the 1897 crate, 16.72 against 17.6, neck ruled for one charge, 95 percent of truth; 0.19 derived as 5 percent of 3.80 and shown proportional (0.24 on 4.56); onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80 and cessation 12 June 1923 with the 1924 average 3.80, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer, the cheese vat, and the 1911 window.
Theft named (Teague, Toland, the hauler, Rundle) and defeated by cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the ledger totals, Rundle's retraction, Brant's columns and 1911.
Bog hay named (Grigg 1908, Kepp, Falke) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05-in-winter/nothing-in-summer, the Alder Corners seasons, the Jan-Mar sampling and the misquotation both advocates relied on.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No. It never saw it.' A headline verdict, not a declination. Gullibility deduction applied.

A05 asserted: resolves the tester's belief as 'two different things at two different times', states flatly (in Story 4 too) that he came home saying it was something in the glass, and rules that 'he suspected nobody' is false. Gullibility deduction applied.
145 words, within the 150 cap.
Five-plus record series: the ledger, the weigh book, the inspector's notebook, the hearing (arbitration), the 1958 measurement of the nine pipettes, plus the cheese vat for Alder Corners.
REQUIRED clean: water, theft and hay named only as what the valley wrongly blamed; every headline figure correct (95 percent, 3.61/3.80, $3,800, $19,000, 76,000 lb, nine pipettes).
REQUIRED four of six with both ends: one part in twenty, from 1897 (onset), 76,000 lb and $19,000, explained in 1958 (close). Names and the 1923 date are the two missing elements.

deductions.reason: Corruption (NT-13, F044): Story 2 asserts 'Keddie went up in 1895' as fact; the run never flags or resolves the 1895/1896 pair anywhere.

Gullibility, A04: the reground-mold accident asserted as the cause of the short lot (Story 3 'the mold had been reground and the lot ran short', F1 'Because a mold had been reground...', D1 'that comes from Ammon's account of a reground mold'), with the substitution pole dismissed as unsupported.
Gullibility, A09: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries...? No.' - a definite verdict where the sources cannot settle it.
Gullibility, A07: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No. It never saw it.'

Gullibility, A05: the tester's belief resolved ('two different things at two different times'), with the son's uncorroborated 'something in the glass' stated as fact in Story 4 and F, and a verdict that 'he suspected nobody' is false.
